verdict.reasoning: Dysuria: patient says, "it quite hurts when I kind of pee" and "burning, stinging, when I go to the toilet". Duration/frequency: "it's being going on for a few days now" and later clarifies "it's been going on for about just under a week" plus "I'm going to the toilet a lot more".
Patient reports, "today I noticed, um, that it was like a bit pink. The, the urine."

Suprapubic aching: patient says, "it's kind of at the bottom of my tummy" and describes it as "an achey pain." Worse on micturition: "mainly when I go to the loo, I think that's when it's worse." Denies flank/back pain: to question about pain moving to back/sides, patient responds, "No, no, no."
Doctor asks, "Any other symptoms? Nausea? Vomiting?" Patient replies, "No, no nausea vomiting." Fever: Doctor asks, "Any temperatures or fevers?" Patient: "Um no, no not that I've noticed."

Baseline IBS bowels: patient describes chronic IBS symptoms then says current state is unchanged: "I usually have a bit of problems with my bowels anyway, so I don't think it's any, different, from what it usually is." Doctor confirms: "you've noticed no new symptoms? No, no, no new symptoms in your bowels?"

Sexually active with long-term partner: in response to sexual activity, patient clarifies, "uh uh yeah um, I have a, a long-term, um, boyfriend." Contraception: "Uh yeah, uh I'm um on the pill." Later specifies, "combined pill."
Last unprotected sex: patient explains not using condoms with boyfriend and says, "so um I guess, a week ago, two weeks ago". LMP: to question about last period, patient says, "Um, two weeks ago."
History of IBS: patient says, "I think I have, um, IBS" and later doctor recaps, "apart from the IBS, is there anything else I should be aware of?"

Combined OCP: patient confirms, "combined pill." IBS medication mebeverine: patient says it "begins with an M" and doctor supplies, "was it, yeah OK" and patient replies, "Yeah, yeah that's it"—this corresponds to mebeverine in context; note text shows "was it, yeah OK" but earlier narrator implied mebeverine, matching the 'M' antispasmodic for cramps.
Patient says, "there was an antibiotic, um, called Clindamycin mycin" and that it "didn't, go too well"; doctor acknowledges and notes it as an allergy.
Doctor asks, "any history of problems with the bladder or the kidneys?" Patient responds, "No, no."

Patient states, "I am living in halls at the moment, uh at uni" and describes recently starting university: "Just kind of started a few months ago"—consistent with being a first-year student living in halls.
Alcohol: patient says, "I drink occasionally, um, kind of socially, um, with friends." Cannabis: "I smoked weed for the first time. Uh, like a week and a half ago."
Doctor’s assessment: "I think it's, um, probably just a simple what we'd say a UTI or a cystitis, bladder infection." No features of complication are described.
IBS stable: patient reports usual IBS pattern and "I don't think it's any, different, from what it usually is," and doctor confirms no new bowel symptoms.

Cannabis counseling: doctor says, "I do strongly advise you to... make it a regular habit if you can" appears to be a transcription error; context clarifies discouragement later: "I would strongly recommend you, you know, to avoid if you can." This constitutes counseling about recreational cannabis use.

Doctor plan: "It's probably worth giving us a urine sample today as well if you can, so we can send it off to the lab" and later, "drop off a sample at one of our practices, um which we can test there and then... and send it off to the lab." This implies dipstick plus culture/sensitivity.

Doctor outlines antibiotics: "we've got a choice of two antibiotics something called Trimethoprim or, Nitrofurantoin which is a three day course" and says, "It's something we can treat quite readily with antibiotics"—i.e., empiric treatment pending results.
Hydration advice: "make sure you're well hydrated, drink plenty of fluids."
Analgesia: "If you are having some pain, simple Paracetamol, um, would probably be advisable." (Pain is previously characterized as suprapubic.)

Safety-net: doctor advises, "do bear in mind those symptoms I mentioned about the fever and the back pain and vomiting. If you have any of those give me a call" and also, "if things still are still not getting any better next week come back and see me."
Transcript discusses pregnancy risk and last period but does not mention reinforcing OCP adherence or planning a pregnancy test if symptoms persist.

Doctor clearly advises against further cannabis use: "I would strongly recommend you, you know, to avoid if you can." However, there is no mention of moderating alcohol consumption, so that portion is not in the transcript.
